hypotheses.justification: The statement never uses a measurable space on the adele ring. `ν` lives on the units `(AdeleRing (𝓞 F) F)ˣ`, which has its own `MeasurableSpace` binder. `ideleNorm` is defined through `distribHaarChar`, which does not take measurable-space arguments on the ring (its body builds `borel A` internally). `schwartzBruhat`, `ThetaSum` and `IsFundamentalDomain` don't use it either. The only use is in the proof, where `ideleNorm_mul_principal` takes `[MeasurableSpace 𝔸] [BorelSpace 𝔸]`. That lemma uses them only because `NumberField.AdeleRing.distribHaarChar_algebraMap` takes them as arguments, and the conclusion `distribHaarChar … = 1` doesn't depend on them. The theorem can supply them itself: start the proof with `letI := NumberField.AdelicHaar.adeleBorel (𝓞 F) F; haveI := NumberField.AdelicHaar.borelSpace_adeleBorel (𝓞 F) F`. `adeleBorel` is `borel _`, and `borelSpace_adeleBorel` is `BorelSpace.mk rfl`. Both are in Definitions/Def_NumberField_AdelicHaar.lean. The rest of the proof (`integrable_zetaIntegrand`, `integral_eq_setIntegral_tsum_smul`, `chi_mul_principal`) never touches these instances. So the statement stays true and provable without them. This and the `BorelSpace` binder below can be removed together, because the same two `letI`/`haveI` lines replace both.

Same reasoning as for the `MeasurableSpace` binder on the adele ring. Nothing in the statement refers to a Borel structure on the ring itself; the `BorelSpace` instance needed for `ν` is the one on the units. The proof uses it only to call `ideleNorm_mul_principal`. That call can be served by `haveI := NumberField.AdelicHaar.borelSpace_adeleBorel (𝓞 F) F`, paired with `letI := NumberField.AdelicHaar.adeleBorel (𝓞 F) F`. The quantity `ideleNorm F x` doesn't depend on these instances. So the binder can be deleted and the theorem keeps the same statement. This can be removed together with the `MeasurableSpace` binder, which the same two lines also replace.
